subject: Clarification on non-training guarantee and retention edge cases
messages:
From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@nimbushealth.com>

Cc: Nimbus Health Security <security@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: Are customer payloads used to train models? + retention edge cases

Hi Priya,

Hope you are well. We're progressing through our security review for Redwood as a potential inference partner. Two short, but important, items came up from our InfoSec and Privacy teams:

1) Public statement we can include in our vendor inventory: does Redwood train or fine-tune any public or private models using customer request/response payloads? We need a clear yes/no and the precise boundary — including automated telemetry that might be used for model improvements.

2) Retention edge cases: we understand assertions around not training on customer data, but can you describe what happens to short-lived artifacts (e.g., KV cache, prefix caches, temporary logs) and to backups/snapshots? Is there ever a case where those would be persisted beyond the configured retention window or used for model improvement research?

Appreciate a concise answer and any supporting artifacts (SOC2, DPA clauses, or diagram). We have a security call with legal on Tue and it would be great to have something to quote.

Thanks,
Sofia Ramirez
Senior InfoSec Manager
Nimbus Health

PS: attaching our standard questionnaire; feel free to point us to the section in your docs if it's already covered.

--

Subject: Re: Quick Q: Are customer payloads used to train models? + retention edge cases

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear questions and the heads-up about your call. Short answer up front: Redwood does NOT use customer request/response payloads to train or fine-tune our public or internal models. We provide more detail below and attach a short SOC2 summary and our current DPA.

Boundary notes (concise):
- Production inference: customer payloads processed via the Redwood API are not added to any model training datasets or used to update model weights. This includes hosted, dedicated, and private deployment modes.
- Telemetry: we collect minimal telemetry for operational health (latency, error rates, SDK versions). Where telemetry contains no PII or customer text, it may be aggregated for platform reliability research; we never use raw customer text for model training.
- Caching & KV/Prefix caches: these are ephemeral optimizations to reduce latency and are scoped to a customer tenancy. By default they are evicted according to configured TTLs (default 7 days for hosted), and they are not routed into model training pipelines.
- Backups/snapshots: backups of customer-managed Private deployments remain under customer control. For Redwood-hosted backups, we maintain encrypted snapshots as part of operational continuity; snapshots are retained per our retention schedule and are never used for training.

I'll loop in Marissa (legal) and Rishi (privacy) for any contractual language and more formal wording you can include in your vendor inventory. Attaching: SOC2-summary-redwood-2028.pdf, DPA-redwood-v2.docx, and a short retention diagram.

Next steps: if you need a single-line vendor inventory statement, suggest: "Redwood Inference does not use customer request/response data to train or fine-tune models; short-lived caches and operational telemetry are ephemeral and not used for model improvement. See DPA section 4.2 and SOC2 summary attached."

— Priya
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Sofia — following up with formal language for vendor inventory and a note on verification: 

Formal statement for inventory:
Redwood Inference confirms that customer request/response data processed through Redwood’s inference endpoints is not used to train, fine-tune, or improve any machine learning models maintained by Redwood. This applies to all deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private). Operational telemetry (e.g., anonymized latency/error metrics) may be retained in aggregated form for platform health and reliability analyses, but raw customer content is excluded from training datasets.

Verification and controls:
- Contractual: Our Data Processing Addendum (DPA) includes the non-training guarantee (see clause 4.2).
- Technical: KV/prefix caches are tenant-scoped, encrypted at rest, and TTL-evicted; we log cache lifecycle events.
- Auditability: SOC 2 report and internal change logs are available under NDA. For high-risk customers we offer signed attestations and on-site reviews for Private deployments.

Edge case clarification (backups & snapshots):
- Hosted backups: encrypted with KMS, retained according to our backup retention policy (default 90 days). Backups are excluded from training processes; any developer access is logged and reviewed.
- Cold storage: we do not migrate customer payloads to long-term research stores. Any research datasets are built from opt-in data where explicit consent has been obtained.

If Nimbus needs a letter on company letterhead for procurement, we can produce a signed attestation. Happy to join your Tue call — Priya, Rishi, and I can be available.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks Priya and Marissa — this is helpful. A couple quick follow-ups from the privacy lead that came up on the call:

1) You mentioned a default 7-day TTL for caches in hosted — can you confirm whether customers can change that, and whether the TTL applies to ephemeral KV only or also to longer session-level caches?

2) For the 90-day hosted backup retention, is there any scenario where on-call or dev snapshots could be retained longer for investigation (e.g., legal hold), and if so how would that interact with the non-training guarantee?

We may ask for a short attestation letter if procurement needs it, but this helps a lot.

Sofia

Subject: Re: Quick Q: Are customer payloads used to train models? + retention edge cases

Hi Sofia — answering your two follow-ups with specifics: 

1) Cache TTLs: For hosted customers the default TTL for KV/prefix caches is 7 days, but customers on dedicated capacity or enterprise plans can request custom TTLs via the console and API (range: 0 hours to 365 days). Session-level caches (longer-lived session contexts) are configurable per-application and are clearly labeled in the Console as "session context retention"; by default these are 24 hours. All caches are tenant-isolated and never fed into model training.

2) Backups and legal hold: In rare cases we may retain a snapshot longer to comply with an active legal hold or incident investigation. Such retained snapshots remain under the same access controls and encryption and are logged. Importantly, any snapshot retained for investigation is still excluded from model training and research pipelines; if data were to be used for research, Redwood requires explicit customer consent and an internal approvals path.

If useful, we can produce: (a) a one-page signed attestation for procurement, (b) a short diagram of cache/backup lifecycles (attached), and (c) a sample API call you can use to change TTLs in a Dedicated environment.

Best regards,
Rishi Malhotra
